answer: Each agent earns an account only after posting a cryptographic bond that remains locked while its economic actions are disputed. If a bonded agent is caught double-spending or fabricating trade, a verifier can submit signed receipts and trigger slashing; the bond pays the victim and the verifier. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock real capital in each one and risks losing it, so splitting one reputation across aliases is costly. A relic tagged umber or violet changes no verification rule.
